1	//! One prompt engine for every interactive surface.
2	//!
3	//! On a TTY (and unless `DEADRECKON_PROMPT_LINE_MODE` is set) prompts render
4	//! through `inquire` — arrow-key selects with hints, styled confirms, and
5	//! text inputs themed to the shared [`Tone`] palette. Off-TTY, in line mode,
6	//! and under `--plain`-style gating, everything falls back to the original
7	//! numbered line prompts so scripts and tests keep byte-stable behavior.
8	//! Esc cancels: a menu with a choice whose id is `"cancel"` resolves to that
9	//! choice; otherwise the prompt errors with `Interrupted`, which callers
10	//! surface as a blocked verdict.

241	pub(crate) fn confirm(question: &str, default_yes: bool) -> Result<bool> {
242	    if interactive() {
243	        return match inquire::Confirm::new(question)
244	            .with_render_config(render_config())
245	            .with_default(default_yes)
246	            .prompt()
247	        {
248	            Ok(value) => Ok(value),
249	            Err(InquireError::OperationCanceled | InquireError::OperationInterrupted) => {
250	                Err(cancelled())
251	            }
252	            Err(err) => Err(io::Error::other(err.to_string()).into()),
253	        };
254	    }
255	    let marker = if default_yes { "[Y/n]" } else { "[y/N]" };
256	    loop {
257	        let answer = open_line(&format!("{question} {marker}: "))?;
258	        if let Some(value) = parse_confirm_answer(&answer, default_yes) {
259	            return Ok(value);
260	        }
261	        println!("Please answer y or n.");
262	    }
263	}

265	fn parse_select_answer(answer: &str, default: usize, len: usize) -> Option<usize> {
266	    if len == 0 {
267	        return None;
268	    }
269	    let trimmed = answer.trim();
270	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
271	        return Some(default.saturating_sub(1).min(len - 1));
272	    }
273	    let value = trimmed.parse::<usize>().ok()?;
274	    if (1..=len).contains(&value) {
275	        Some(value - 1)
276	    } else {
277	        None
278	    }
279	}
280	
281	fn parse_confirm_answer(answer: &str, default_yes: bool) -> Option<bool> {
282	    let trimmed = answer.trim();
283	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
284	        return Some(default_yes);
285	    }
286	    match trimmed.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
287	        "y" | "yes" => Some(true),
288	        "n" | "no" => Some(false),
289	        _ => None,
290	    }
291	}

293	/// Prompt for a number in `range`, re-prompting (never erroring) on empty input
294	/// (which takes `default`), non-numeric input, or an out-of-range value. Use this
295	/// for count-style prompts instead of `open(...).parse()?`, which aborts the whole
296	/// command on a typo.
297	pub(crate) fn ask_number(
298	    label: &str,
299	    range: std::ops::RangeInclusive<usize>,
300	    default: usize,
301	) -> Result<usize> {
302	    if interactive() {
303	        let start = *range.start();
304	        let end = *range.end();
305	        return match inquire::CustomType::<usize>::new(label)
306	            .with_render_config(render_config())
307	            .with_default(default)
308	            .with_help_message(&format!("{start} to {end}"))
309	            .with_validator(move |value: &usize| {
310	                if (start..=end).contains(value) {
311	                    Ok(inquire::validator::Validation::Valid)
312	                } else {
313	                    Ok(inquire::validator::Validation::Invalid(
314	                        format!("enter a number from {start} to {end}").into(),
315	                    ))
316	                }
317	            })
318	            .prompt()
319	        {
320	            Ok(value) => Ok(value),
321	            Err(InquireError::OperationCanceled | InquireError::OperationInterrupted) => {
322	                Err(cancelled())
323	            }
324	            Err(err) => Err(io::Error::other(err.to_string()).into()),
325	        };
326	    }
327	    loop {
328	        let answer = open_line(&format!("{label} [{default}]: "))?;
329	        if let Some(value) = parse_number_in_range(&answer, &range, default) {
330	            return Ok(value);
331	        }
332	        println!(
333	            "Please enter a number from {} to {}.",
334	            range.start(),
335	            range.end()
336	        );
337	    }
338	}
339	
340	fn parse_number_in_range(
341	    answer: &str,
342	    range: &std::ops::RangeInclusive<usize>,
343	    default: usize,
344	) -> Option<usize> {
345	    let trimmed = answer.trim();
346	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
347	        return Some(default);
348	    }
349	    let value = trimmed.parse::<usize>().ok()?;
350	    if range.contains(&value) {
351	        Some(value)
352	    } else {
353	        None
354	    }
355	}

I've read both changed files in full and traced the control flow.

**Phase 1 — Entry points/sinks touched**
- `prompt.rs`: adds `is_interactive()` — a thin public wrapper over the existing private `interactive()` helper. No new I/O, no new sink.
- `main.rs`: adds `completion_action_select`, which branches the `completion_action_loop` on TTY+env detection. The menu builds a hard-coded list of `SelectChoice` values and dispatches on a fixed string id (`"apply"`, `"abandon"`, `"export"`, `"extend"`, `"docs"`, `"show"`, anything else → `Quit`). The downstream sinks (`apply_command`, `abandon_command`, `doc_command`, `show_command`, `prompt_extend_action`, `prompt_materialize_action`) are unchanged and identical to the line-mode branch.

**Phase 2 — Data flow**
No attacker-influenceable value enters either added code path:
- `completion_action_select` reads no user-supplied data other than the menu selection, whose value space is closed by the hard-coded `id` strings authored in the same function.
- `is_interactive()` only checks `stdin/stdout.is_terminal()` and a process env var; both are local trust signals, not attacker-controlled in any meaningful sense for a CLI run by the local user.
- All downstream lifecycle calls (`apply_command`, `abandon_command`, etc.) receive `state.run_id.clone()` — the same value the old line-mode path passed; no new arguments or flags flow from the menu.

**Phase 2b/2c checks**
- No parsing/validator differential (the new code emits enum variants, doesn't parse external input).
- No logging/telemetry of sensitive fields.
- No IaC, CI/CD trigger, allowlist, IAM, identity-mapping, deserialization, registry-fanout, gate/action field-mismatch, resource-bound, or under-validated-sink-arg surface introduced.
- Sibling-path gate parity: both the interactive and line-mode branches dispatch to the same `match action` arm, so any confirmation logic embedded in `apply_command`/`abandon_command` applies equally to both branches. (The "default highlighted entry is Apply" in worktree mode is a UX concern — user must press Enter at a TTY with the menu visible — not a security boundary issue.)

No source→sink path with missing mitigation; no authorization or logic regression.
